newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebel leader shows personality amid garbage.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel leader shows personality amid garbage.

text.p: Police gathering intelligence on the leader of Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages have found clues to his personality in garbage at the siege site in Lima, according to a police document obtained by Reuters.

Rebel leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini is self-controlled, rational, and would prefer to end the siege peacefully, according to the report, which analysed handwritten notes found in garbage collected by the Red Cross at the Japanese ambassador's residence.

But for the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) leader, who led the storming of the diplomatic mansion on Dec. 17, "satisfying his ego is a powerful sentiment that feeds his motivation," the three-page report said.
Cerpa is "difficult to negotiate with so long as he feels in control" and "completely untrustworthy" if he is in a weak position, according to the police handwriting analysts.
The rebel leader has been locked for almost four months in negotiations with the government to resolve the crisis.

Sources close to the talks say they have lately been focused on the rebels' demand of freedom for imprisoned comrades in exchange for their 72 captives. Peru President Alberto Fujimori has publicly ruled out releasing any MRTA prisoners.
Cerpa, a former trade union leader, led about 20 MRTA rebels into the Japanese ambassador's home during a cocktail party and took 500 guests hostage.
All but 72 were released, most of them in the early days of the crisis. Among the remaining hostages are Peru's foreign minister, Fujimori's brother and several Japanese businessmen.
The police report said Cerpa was prepared to wait "a long time" without making a decision, and he does not necessarily solve problems through violence.
"He probably wants to be remembered as a hero that achieved his goals without bloodshed," the report concluded.
